name: Delaware
summary: Statutes: delcode.delaware.gov (official) — section text sits on the subchapter page, or on the chapter page when a chapter has no subchapters; Justia 2025 is a constructible tier-2 fallback. Constitution: delcode.delaware.gov per-article pages. Court rules are full-set PDFs on courts.delaware.gov that the fetch tool cuts off after ~100K characters; read them from the corpus (Superior Court Criminal Rules ingested 2026-10-16) or with fetch_doc.py. Admin Code: regulations.delaware.gov is a JavaScript app (the fetch tool gets an empty shell) with a public JSON API and PDF downloads; Cornell LII mirrors it per section. Case law: the courts.delaware.gov opinion database (Supreme Court from 1998, Chancery and Superior from 2000) is searchable by a plain GET URL and serves slip-opinion PDFs that fetch_doc.py reads in full; Justia covers older Supreme Court and Chancery opinions.

citation_map.notes: Supr. Ct. R. 14(g) mandates Bluebook form with no parallel state-reporter cite (A.2d/A.3d only) and gives the Delaware unreported form 'Name, Del., No. N, YYYY, Judge, J. (date)'. Del. and Del. Ch. official reporters ended long ago (Del. Ch. vol. 43, 1968; Del. vol. 59, 1966, per memory); modern Delaware cases are cited to A.2d/A.3d or WL/LEXIS. Many Chancery and Superior decisions are never in A.3d and are cited by WL number plus C.A. No.; a WL number cannot be resolved to a free URL: search by party name in the courts.delaware.gov database or Justia instead. Chancery C.A. Nos. take the form YYYY-NNNN-XXX (judge initials suffix, sometimes omitted). Supreme Court dockets take the form 'No. N, YYYY' (filing year). CourtListener court ids are from memory and unverified. Routing caution: 'No. N, YYYY' and bare C.A. numbers are Delaware forms but can collide with other courts' docket styles; route on them only with Delaware context. Westlaw cites route here only with a '(Del.' parenthetical. DGCL = Title 8, chapter 1 (8 Del. C. § 101 et seq.). A '§§ a-b' range is a span of sections, not a hyphenated section: the regex refuses it, so take the first section. Bare 'Section N of Title T' is context_required: Maine uses the same prose form (split 2026-10-17).

sources.title: Delaware Code Online
sources.publisher: Delaware Code Revisors / Division of Legislative Services (prepared with LexisNexis)
sources.official_status_evidence: Home page notice (https://delcode.delaware.gov/index.html) says the online Code 'is considered an official version of the State of Delaware statutory code'; UELMA-authenticated per-title PDFs (e.g. /title8/title8.pdf) also available.
sources.coverage: All 31 titles of the Delaware Code; per-title authenticated PDFs; HTML by chapter/subchapter.

access.pattern_rules: title = plain integer, no padding (title5, title10, title29). Chapter folder = 'c' + 3-digit zero-padded chapter number + lower-case letter suffix if any (c018, c081, c002a, c012d); some odd slugs exist (title6 'c012_1' = Chapter 12 False Claims Act, 'c000a' = UCC Article A) so always confirm via the title index. Hyphenated sections give the chapter directly (6 Del. C. § 18-101 → c018). Non-hyphenated sections (8 Del. C. § 141, 5 Del. C. § 952, 10 Del. C. § 8106) do not encode the chapter: the title and chapter index pages show NO section ranges. Infer the chapter from the section's leading digits — sections numbered NNN or NNNN sit in chapter floor(section/100) (5 § 952 → c009, 8 § 141 → c001, 10 § 8106 → c081, 19 § 710 → c007) — then open that chapter page and confirm the anchor id="{section}" exists (on the chapter page or one of its subchapter pages). If it is not there, use de-code-justia's chapter listing, which does show section ranges, to find the right chapter; never keep guessing. If a chapter has subchapters, the chapter index.html is navigation-only and lists sc01..scNN links (two-digit, Arabic, even though headings say Subchapter IV); the subchapter page holds the text. If a chapter has NO subchapters (e.g. title10/c081), the chapter index.html itself holds the section text. Sections are anchored by id equal to the section number (id="18-101", id="141", id="8106").
access.navigation: title index → chapter link (cNNN) → if the page lists sc links, follow the subchapter covering the section → section text with anchor #{section}. Examples verified: 6 Del. C. § 18-101 → /title6/c018/sc01/index.html; 5 Del. C. § 952 → /title5/c009/sc02/index.html; 8 Del. C. § 141 → /title8/c001/sc04/index.html; 10 Del. C. § 8106 → /title10/c081/index.html (no subchapters).

automation.notes: WebFetch truncates at ~100,000 characters with '[Content truncated due to length...]'; large subchapter pages (e.g. 11 Del. C. ch. 5 subch. II, ~154K chars of text, §§ 601-792) lose later sections: § 791 NOT PRESENT even with offset=100000 (that window ended at § 778). For such pages use the shell (curl + strip tags, anchor id) or Justia's per-section page.

WebFetch reads ~100K characters per page; on very large subchapter pages later sections can be unreachable even with offset (11 Del. C. § 791) — use de-code-justia's per-section page for those.

sources.title: Delaware Supreme Court appeals in the Opinions and Orders database
sources.coverage: The Delaware Supreme Court is the only appellate court (no intermediate court; Chancery and Superior appeals go directly to it as of right). Affirmances by order and opinions both appear in the opinions database with a '(Court of Chancery)' / '(Superior Court)' court-below tag. US Supreme Court certiorari is the only further review.

access.pattern_rules: Search by GET (verified by WebFetch and shell 2026-10-16): https://courts.delaware.gov/opinions/index.aspx?ag={court}&period=year&year={YYYY}&results=25&ss={search}&page=1 — court = 'Supreme Court' | 'Court of Chancery' | 'Superior Court' | 'Family Court' | 'Court of Common Pleas' | 'All Courts' (URL-encode spaces); search is a substring match on party name or docket and is limited to the chosen year. Rows give case name, date, docket (Supreme 'N, YYYY'; Chancery 'C.A. No. YYYY-NNNN-XXX'), court below, judge, and the download id; the PDF is https://courts.delaware.gov/opinions/download.aspx?id={id}. The id is not derivable — take it from the result row. Searching a trial-court C.A. number does not find the Supreme Court appeal: search the party name in the Supreme Court for the year(s) after the trial decision; the order/opinion names the court below and its C.A. No. Substring search also returns unrelated parties sharing a word — confirm the C.A. No. in the PDF.
access.navigation: GET search URL → result row → download.aspx?id={id} PDF

hazards: party-name search only; parties often reversed on appeal (appellant first)
docket search on lower C.A. No. fails
Justia lists only opinions/orders it has ingested

No. 2023-0309-JTL; Supreme 2026 search 'Moelis' → id 390230, '340, 2024', '(Court of Chancery)'; PDF caption 'Court Below: Court of Chancery … C.A. sources.notes: Delaware also accepts certified questions (Supr. Ct. R. 41) and interlocutory appeals (Supr. Ct. R. 42); both are decided by the Supreme Court and appear in the same database. Interlocutory-appeal refusals are issued as orders.

script_candidates.why: Public JSON API: GET /api/AdminCode/titles, POST /api/AdminCode/title and /api/AdminCode/regulation {regulationUrl} returning htmlBody + pdfId; GET /api/file/download/{id}. A small script turns '14 DE Admin. Code 101' into text deterministically, bypassing the SPA.
GET /api/register/monthlyRegister lists every issue since 1997 with pdfFileId/textFileId; RSS at /api/register/regs-rss.xml.

ASP.NET POST search (court, year, free text) returns structured rows (name, date, docket, court below, judge, description, download id) — a script can resolve (court, docket/party, year) → PDF id and also find Supreme Court appeals for subsequent history.

Static HTML with id-anchored sections; a script can build a section→(chapter, subchapter) map from the 31 title indexes once, making all citations constructible and avoiding WebFetch truncation on large subchapter pages.
